paper_title: Enhancement of the Photoresponse in Organic Field-Effect Transistors by Incorporating Thin DNA Layers

knowledge_points.content: The study utilizes DNA as a thin functional layer integrated into organic field-effect transistors (OFETs) to enhance their photoresponse.
knowledge_points.evidence: Enhancement of the Photoresponse in Organic Field-Effect Transistors by Incorporating Thin DNA Layers... PCBDR/DNA films

knowledge_points.content: PCBDR is used as the active organic semiconductor material in the fabrication of the organic phototransistors.
knowledge_points.evidence: Dark output... and transfer... characteristics of PCBDR and PCBDR/DNA OFETs

knowledge_points.content: X-ray photoemission spectroscopy (XPS) confirms the presence of DNA in PCBDR/DNA films by detecting P 2p and Na 1s photoelectrons, which are characteristic elements of the DNA backbone and its counter-ions.
knowledge_points.evidence: Figure S2. X-ray photoemission spectroscopy of the PCBDR and PCBDR/DNA films in zoomed-in range for (a) P 2p and (b) Na 1s photoelectrons.

knowledge_points.content: The incorporation of a DNA layer shifts the threshold voltage (Vth) and turn-on voltage (Von) of PCBDR-based OFETs, and these parameters are dependent on the work function of the source-drain electrodes (e.g., Au or Al).
knowledge_points.evidence: Figure S4. (c) Threshold voltage (Vth) and turn-on voltage (Von) of PCBDR OFETs with and without the DNA layer as a function of the electrode WF.

knowledge_points.content: The incorporation of DNA into PCBDR OFETs significantly enhances the drain current under illumination compared to dark conditions, indicating an improved photoresponse.
knowledge_points.evidence: Figure S5. Comparison of dark and illuminated (a), (b) output (Vg = 60 V) and (c), (d) transfer (Vd = 12 V) characteristics of PCBDR control (left panels) and PCBDR/DNA (right panels) devices

knowledge_points.content: Scanning Kelvin probe microscopy is employed to determine the work function (WF) of the metal electrodes (Au and Al) used in the organic phototransistors.
knowledge_points.evidence: Figure S3. Work function (WF) of metals used for the OPT electrodes determined by scanning Kelvin probe microscopy.

knowledge_points.content: Electrostatic Force Microscopy (EFM) is used to measure the contact potential difference between the tip and the sample surface for both PCBDR and PCBDR/DNA films.
knowledge_points.evidence: Figure S1. 1ω EFM (2 μm × 2 μm) of (a) PCBDR and (b) PCBDR/DNA films with applying a Vdc = -0.28 V that cancels out the contact potential difference

knowledge_points.content: The steady-state absorbance spectra of PCBDR and PCBDR/DNA films remain similar, suggesting that the incorporation of the thin DNA layer does not significantly alter the optical absorption properties of the bulk PCBDR film.
knowledge_points.evidence: Figure S6. Steady-state absorbance of PCBDR and PCBDR/DNA films which are prepared identically to those used in devices.

knowledge_points.content: The study evaluates OFET performance in the linear regime with a drain voltage (Vd) of 12 V and a gate voltage (Vg) up to 60 V.
knowledge_points.evidence: Figure S4. (a) Dark output (Vg = 60 V) and (b) transfer (linear regime, Vd = 12 V) characteristics

knowledge_points.content: Device dimensions for the characterized OFETs include a channel width (Wch) of 1 mm and a channel length (Lch) of 70 μm.
